title: The Writer Who Invented Cyberpunk Never Played a Game
summary: William Gibson is a very important science fiction writer. His book Neuromancer, from the 1980s, helped create cyberpunk, a kind of story about hackers, high-tech cities, and virtual worlds. But here is the funny part: Gibson says he has never played a video game in his life. 'I've never played a video game in my life, but this thing [Grand Theft Auto] actually does [seem] interesting,' Gibson wrote this weekend. He only found a clip interesting in its 'texture' or 'depth.' Gibson built his imaginary worlds by watching real life. In the 1970s, he spent time around arcades in Vancouver, Canada, watching teens near the game machines. From that, he invented the idea of 'cyberspace,' a word gamers and writers still use today. Now the new game Grand Theft Auto VI has caught his eye, at least as a viewer. One clip shows a boom barrier throwing a character named Jason into the air like a catapult. Another shows a dog driving a jetski to save Jason. If early sales numbers are true, Grand Theft Auto VI is the best-selling piece of media of all time.
why_it_matters: The games you play were shaped by writers like Gibson, even if he never played one himself.
